topics.topic: Precedence between channel_over_bound and deadline timeout outcomes
questions: Must channel_over_bound always conclude resource_exhausted, or does timeout take precedence when the deadline also passed?

quotes: When cleanup was confirmed the outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the report's resource_hit is true — the runner hit its memory, process or scratch limit, the scratch limit being the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant, which runner_arguments writes as file_size_limit into the runner's command line and which is no field of ResourceBounds or RunnerLaunch —, the observation's channel_over_bound holds, or the output count exceeds bounds.output_bytes; sandbox_violation when the report holds any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the report says crashed, the runner exited abnormally, or no returned message was read — the report's returned is None: read_runner_report always gives a RunnerReport, for a channel that carried nothing one with no trap hit, no resource hit, crashed false, failure None and returned None, so the observation always holds a report; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded.
judgement.why: The ordered outcome rule makes timeout precede resource_exhausted when both the deadline and channel bound are observed.

topics.topic: Precedence between channel_over_bound and unconfirmed-cleanup failure outcomes
questions: Must channel_over_bound conclude resource_exhausted even when cleanup is unconfirmed, or must cleanup_failed override it with crashed?

quotes: When cleanup was not confirmed the outputs are discarded and the result is outcome crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed of = models.DetailCode, whatever else was observed.
judgement.why: The cleanup rule explicitly overrides every other observation, including channel_over_bound.

topics.topic: Whether reach_operation_element must request a fresh approval after a not_applied resolution or may reuse an existing requested approval
questions: Must reach_operation_element always create a fresh approval after a not_applied resolution, or must it reuse any existing requested approval as currently specified?

After a not_applied resolution, must reach_operation_element always request a fresh approval, or must it reuse any existing requested approval even when that approval predates the resolved attempt or has a different request_digest?

Must reach_operation_element always request a new approval after not_applied, or must it reuse any existing requested approval even when that approval predates the resolved attempt and cannot count as resend authority?

quotes: otherwise — no NodeExecution, or a latest outcome_unknown whose attempt the owner resolved not_applied — the element is not reached, so it is reached again when its node is next taken, and after not_applied its send needs a fresh approval (find_send_authority), which reach_operation_element requests (decision 32).

When find_send_authority returns None MUST, unless an approval of the element with status requested already exists, write one RequestApprovalChange for the element with the binding_id, input_digests, the prepared request_digest and an ApprovalPreview of the operation's service_id, operation_name and effect_class, the prepared request description and the element's input PortRefs; input_digests are the digests of every input value and file in input port name order, list elements in list order.
Nothing is sent and the element waits with reason owner_approval for that approval, the existing requested one when there was one, even if its request_digest differs.
judgement.why: The changed conclusion rule requires a fresh approval after not_applied, while the reach rule requires reuse of any existing requested approval, including one with a different request digest.

topics.topic: Representation of an empty-list mapped operation in plan_run
questions: Must an empty-list mapped operation have the non-position element without map_index, or are all of its elements required to be positions of the delivered list?

quotes: a list with no position gives no element, and a mapped node over an empty list is instead ready with over_empty_list and one element without map_index, which stands for the node and is no position of the list
judgement.why: The text explicitly requires the non-position element without map_index for an empty-list mapped node.
